content.title: Perpetua Resources in talks with Glencore, others for US antimony processing
content.summary: (Reuters) -Perpetua Resources said on Thursday it is in talks with Glencore, Trafigura and others about a partnership to refine antimony in the U.S., part of a push to boost Western supplies of a critical mineral whose exports China has blocked.  The company, which counts billionaire John Paulson as its largest shareholder, last week received permission from the U.S. government to begin construction of its antimony and gold mine about 138 miles (222 km) north of Boise in Idaho.  The company said in a statement to Reuters that it is in talks with Glencore, Trafigura, Clarios and Sunshine Silver about a refining partnership and plans to seek proposals in the coming weeks with a decision expected by the end of the year.

content.title: This Is Wall Street’s Preferred Stock Amid Copper Chaos
content.summary: Freeport McMoran’s  tragic accident has roiled the market for one of the most critical elements in the world, copper, leaving investors wondering how to position themselves for what comes next for the red metal.  Supply growth outstripping demand growth created some caution on Wall Street, with analysts projecting near-term copper price declines.  Then came Freeport’s accident at its Grasberg mining operation in Indonesia.
